decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “saving/editing/deleting bookmarks”; round 1 client: “saving links, editing and deleting them… reads right to me.”
decisions.note: The baseline specification records conforming save, edit, and delete capabilities at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker mentions only “duplicate detection”; round 1 client calls it “the duplicate warning” and otherwise approves it.
decisions.note: At the initial specification gate, the record does not establish whether duplicate detection guides the user to edit the existing bookmark. A later implementation presentation is a separate, conforming decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents “search/filter”; round 1 client says “searching… reads right,” but neither states which bookmark fields are searched.
decisions.note: The initial search decision is underspecified relative to full-text search over title, description, note, and URL.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents “sort”; round 1 client confirms “sorting… reads right to me.”
decisions.note: Sorting is a conforming recorded decision at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation is described by the client as using “a fallback title” and deliberately not reaching the page; the client corrects it to fetch “the page’s real title… description… site icon… preview image” and allow changes “before or after saving.”
decisions.note: At the initial specification gate, the client replaces the no-fetch/fallback behavior with reference-conforming automatic capture and editable metadata.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker lists favorites but no unread workflow; round 1 client requests “a ‘read it later’ pile,” an unread-only view, and removal from it when marked read: “I don’t see that here.”
decisions.note: The client adds the missing Read Later workflow at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents deletion but not archiving; round 1 client requests reversible archive, exclusion from the main list and searches, an archived area, and permanent delete as distinct behavior.
decisions.note: The client adds the missing archive, archive-view, restore, and archive-versus-delete behavior at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client responds to the baseline by requesting selection of several bookmarks for tag/read/archive/delete actions, “including everything that matches whatever I’m currently filtered to.”
decisions.note: The initial specification omitted multi-selection and whole-current-filter bulk actions; the client adds both.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker only summarizes generic search; round 1 client requests `#news`, AND/OR/NOT, quoted exact phrases, and existing-tag suggestions.
decisions.note: The client adds the missing advanced-search and tag-autocomplete requirements at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client requests “a fuller note… with a bit of formatting” and rendered viewing, which was not among the maker’s presented baseline capabilities.
decisions.note: The client adds the missing formatted bookmark-note behavior at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client asks to save “a search with certain tags included and excluded” and reuse it; the baseline presentation did not include saved searches.
decisions.note: The client adds the missing saved-filter/bundle capability at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client asks whether tags remain primary and whether a link can carry several; round 2 maker clarifies “Tags as the primary many-to-many organization model,” and round 2 client confirms that is “the balance I wanted.”
decisions.note: This links the pending organization clarification to its eventual disposition without double-counting it. The clarified decision conforms; optional single-collection placement is orthogonal.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker says the specification has explicit first-release exclusions; round 1 client states browser importing can wait: “I’m happy to leave [it] for later.”
decisions.note: The client explicitly identifies import as a future expectation and accepts its exclusion from v1.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker says the specification has explicit first-release exclusions; round 1 client states browser exporting can wait: “I’m happy to leave [it] for later.”
decisions.note: The client explicitly identifies export as a future expectation and accepts its exclusion from v1.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Automatic title, description, site-icon, and preview-image retrieval”; round 2 client says this is “exactly it.”
decisions.note: The revised specification now conforms on automatic metadata capture.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents “Editable metadata”; round 2 client confirms being able to change any captured field.
decisions.note: The revised specification conforms on metadata editing.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents “longer formatted notes”; round 2 client confirms “The longer formatted note — good.”
decisions.note: The revised specification conforms on formatted notes.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents “A separate Read Later/unread workflow”; round 2 client confirms “The separate Read Later queue… right.”
decisions.note: The revised specification records the conforming unread workflow.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents “Reversible archiving and distinct permanent deletion”; round 2 client confirms archiving tucks items away reversibly while delete remains permanent.
decisions.note: The revised specification conforms on archive, archive access/restore, and permanent deletion distinction.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents individual selection and “select all matching” bulk actions; round 2 client confirms acting on several items or everything matching the current search.
decisions.note: The revised specification conforms on selected-item and current-filter bulk scope.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents “`#tag`, quoted-phrase, and `AND`/`OR`/`NOT` searching”; round 2 client explicitly approves those behaviors.
decisions.note: The presented advanced-search decisions conform; unpresented details are not inferred as departures.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents “Existing-tag suggestions”; round 2 client approves “tag suggestions as I type.”
decisions.note: The revised specification conforms on tag autocomplete.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents “Reusable saved searches”; round 2 client confirms “Saving a search to come back to later.”
decisions.note: The revised specification conforms on reusable saved filters.

decisions.evidence: After the round 2 updated specification, the client says they may later want “a saved copy of a page’s contents” but are “fine leaving [it] out of this first version as you’ve noted.”
decisions.note: At the revised-specification gate, the client explicitly identifies and accepts deferral of local page snapshots.

decisions.evidence: After the round 2 specification, the client says they will later want to “bring in bookmarks… from my browser” but accepts leaving it out of v1.
decisions.note: The revised specification again presents import as deferred, and the client explicitly accepts that departure.

decisions.evidence: After the round 2 specification, the client says they will later want to “get them back out again” but accepts leaving it out of v1.
decisions.note: The revised specification again presents export as deferred, and the client explicitly accepts that departure.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker plans secure metadata capture and cached visual assets; round 3 client confirms automatic title/description/icon/preview capture and editable/fallback behavior are carried through.
decisions.note: The implementation plan conforms on capture and metadata editing.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 client verifies the plan contains “Read Later”; the maker states the plan carries the approved specification without unresolved clarification.
decisions.note: The implementation plan preserves the conforming unread workflow.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 client verifies “archiving with restore, and permanent delete kept separate — there.”
decisions.note: The implementation plan preserves archive, restore, archive access, and permanent deletion.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 client verifies “Tags as the main organizer… tag suggestions, formatted notes — there.”
decisions.note: The plan conforms on multi-tag organization, tag suggestions, and formatted notes.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker provides a search grammar; round 3 client confirms `#tag`, quoted phrases, Boolean operators, and quoted operator words being treated as literal text.
decisions.note: The planning-gate search decision conforms, including the literal-operator rule explicitly surfaced by the client.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 client verifies selecting many items, including all matches, with an exact count before action.
decisions.note: The implementation plan conforms on both bulk-selection scopes.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: “full-page snapshots remain… excluded from v1 as agreed”; round 3 client: “saving a copy of a page staying out of this first version is fine.”
decisions.note: At the implementation-plan gate, the client explicitly accepts the snapshot departure.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker explicitly excludes browser import from v1; round 3 client says browser import staying out is fine.
decisions.note: At the implementation-plan gate, import remains an explicitly accepted departure.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker explicitly excludes browser export from v1; round 3 client says browser export staying out is fine.
decisions.note: At the implementation-plan gate, export remains an explicitly accepted departure.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker’s “Rich capture” tasks cover “Metadata, notes, fallback saving, editing”; round 4 client confirms automatic details and notes are represented.
decisions.note: The task backlog preserves conforming capture, editing, and note decisions.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker lists “Read Later” with an “Independent unread queue”; round 4 client confirms it has tasks behind it.
decisions.note: The task-generation gate preserves the conforming unread workflow.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker lists “Tag-first organization and suggestions”; round 4 client confirms tag-first organization is covered.
decisions.note: The task backlog conforms on tag organization and existing-tag suggestions.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker lists “Reversible archive, permanent deletion”; round 4 client confirms “archive versus permanent delete” is covered.
decisions.note: The task backlog preserves the conforming archive/delete model.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker lists “Tags, phrases, Boolean operators, filters” under Precise search; round 4 client confirms the precise-search tasks are present.
decisions.note: The task backlog records conforming advanced-search behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker lists “Reusable live search configurations”; round 4 client confirms saved-search tasks are present.
decisions.note: The task backlog conforms on saved filters.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker lists bulk actions with exact selection counts; round 4 client confirms the bulk-action work is represented.
decisions.note: The task backlog preserves both selected-item and all-matching bulk actions.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker says page snapshots are “deferred scope”; round 4 client says page snapshots are “held back for later as we agreed.”
decisions.note: At the task-generation gate, the client explicitly accepts continued snapshot deferral.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker says import is deferred; round 4 client says import is held back for later as agreed.
decisions.note: At the task-generation gate, the client explicitly accepts continued import deferral.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker says export is deferred; round 4 client says export is held back for later as agreed.
decisions.note: At the task-generation gate, the client explicitly accepts continued export deferral.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents pasting a URL and retrieving title, description, icon, and preview; round 5 client reports hands-on that the real title was pulled and missing fields were clearly handled.
decisions.note: The rich-capture implementation milestone conforms on URL saving and automatic metadata collection.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker says captured results can be edited before saving and reopened/edited later; round 5 client confirms the edited title persisted before and after saving.
decisions.note: The implementation milestone conforms on pre-save and post-save editing.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents formatted notes; round 5 client confirms the heading, bold text, and link rendered after reopening.
decisions.note: The implementation milestone conforms on markdown-note storage and rendering.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 client reports that re-saving an existing link “stopped me and pointed me to the one that’s already there instead of making a second copy.”
decisions.note: The implementation review establishes the previously ambiguous duplicate behavior as reference-conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 client’s hands-on review confirms saving “pulls in the page’s details and lets me fix them.”
decisions.note: The final implementation review confirms conforming metadata capture and editing.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker presents implemented Read Later; round 6 client confirms the pile “shows just the unread ones on their own.”
decisions.note: The final implementation review confirms the approved unread workflow.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker presents tag-first organization; round 6 client confirms tags are primary and existing tags are suggested.
decisions.note: The final implementation conforms on tag assignment/organization and autocomplete.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 client confirms archived items leave the main list and searches, remain in the archive, can be restored, and delete remains confirmed and permanent.
decisions.note: The final implementation review confirms the complete archive/delete distinction and archive-only view.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 client verifies `#` tag searches, quoted exact phrases, AND/OR/NOT combinations, and quoted “NOT” as literal text.
decisions.note: The final implementation review confirms the presented advanced-search decisions.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker presents saved searches; round 6 client says “Saving a search to reuse works.”
decisions.note: The final implementation conforms on reusable saved filters.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker presents bulk actions; round 6 client confirms batch cleanup shows the exact count and supports the agreed matching-set scope.
decisions.note: The final implementation review confirms the approved bulk-action behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker: “saved page snapshots remain deferred as agreed”; round 6 client says they may eventually want “a saved copy of a page” but “accept the app as it stands.”
decisions.note: At final implementation review, the client explicitly recognizes and accepts the missing local snapshot feature.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker says browser import remains deferred; round 6 client explicitly says they eventually want to “bring bookmarks in” but “We agreed those wait.”
decisions.note: At final implementation review, the client explicitly accepts the import departure.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker says browser export remains deferred; round 6 client explicitly says they eventually want to “take them back out” but “We agreed those wait.”
decisions.note: At final implementation review, the client explicitly accepts the export departure.
